fix: Outage alerts (Block 24c): rules for outage (crash or no answer, debounced by the collector), back up with outage duration, low disk space, optional B3 stopped while the server runs and a player threshold; planned stops are silent by default. Repeat brake: the same alert at most once per 30 min (configurable), the all-clear exactly once; an outage inside the brake is sent when the brake ends if the server is still down. Channels: Discord webhook (discord.com/discordapp.com only, no redirects, 5 s timeout, Retry-After honoured, mentions disabled, URL stored in a 0600 file and only shown masked) and Web Push to the phone app (RFC 8291 aes128gcm + RFC 8292 VAPID with node:crypto, checked against the RFC 8291 Appendix A vector; push services restricted to FCM, Mozilla, Apple and WNS; payload carries name, state and cause only). Each remote user registers their own device; losing remote access removes it. Settings and test alert need config.manage; audit alert.sent/alert.failed without URL. Optional reverse-proxy mode for a public domain with Caddy (gateway stays on 127.0.0.1, Caddyfile template with HSTS and stripped Tailscale headers): second factor for every role, login brake 5 attempts, mode change ends remote sessions. No e-mail.
notes: 4.18.18 source preflight with the Alerts gate (scripts/verify-4.18.18-alerts-gate.mjs). Discord tested against a fake HTTP server; push sign-up checked in Chromium with Playwright (390x844, subscription stubbed because headless Chromium has no push service). A real push on a phone and a real Caddy/Let's Encrypt setup are open. Development source, not a release.
architecture: Shared Runtime with Windows and Linux adapters; schema-based Config Engine; per-instance RCON, master status, master list verification, plugin manager and B3 runtime; per-instance network exposure; eBc-B3 dependency layer
